**Part 3: Visualizing Development Patterns**

**Estimated time:** 2-3 hours

## Before you start

You should be working in your own saved copy of the Posit Cloud project. Use the
same Posit Cloud account every time, write your answers in this `.Rmd` file, and
submit the completed `.Rmd` file to Canvas after it knits.

## Learning goals

By the end of Part 3, you should be able to:

- filter data before plotting;
- make line plots for trends over time;
- choose coherent peer countries for comparisons;
- make scatterplots for descriptive associations;
- label plots clearly; and
- explain why a graph alone is not causal evidence.

## How to work through this file

Each graph should follow the same rhythm: define the goal, create the filtered
data, plot it, check the rows and labels, explain the pattern, and knit before
moving on.

This assignment introduces `ggplot2`, the main plotting system we will use in R.
The goal is descriptive: make graphs that show trends, comparisons, and
associations. Do not claim that one variable causes another.

## Why knit?

Knit regularly. A graph that appears after you run chunks manually might still
fail if the document cannot run from top to bottom.

## Packages and data

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

if (!requireNamespace("tidyverse", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("tidyverse")
}

library(tidyverse)

dev <- read_csv("../data/development_indicators_2026.csv")
dictionary <- read_csv("../data/development_indicators_dictionary_2026.csv")

hks_blue <- "#1F5F83"
hks_crimson <- "#A51C30"
hks_gray <- "#6B7280"

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray35"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
)
```

## A first line plot

A line plot is useful for trends over time. Start by filtering to one country.

```{r}
ghana <- dev |>
  filter(country == "Ghana")

ghana |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_expectancy)) +
  geom_line(color = hks_blue) +
  geom_point(color = hks_blue) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Life expectancy at birth",
    title = "Life Expectancy in Ghana",
    subtitle = "Country-year observations, 2000-2024"
  )
```

## Comparing peer countries

You can use `%in%` to filter to several values at once.

```{r}
east_africa_peers <- dev |>
  filter(country %in% c("Kenya", "Rwanda", "Tanzania", "Uganda"))
```

Check the peer set before plotting it.

```{r}
east_africa_peers |>
  distinct(country, region, income_group) |>
  arrange(country)
```

Map color to country to compare trends.

```{r}
east_africa_peers |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_expectancy, color = country)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Life expectancy at birth",
    color = "Country",
    title = "Life Expectancy Trends Across Four East African Countries"
  )
```

## Scatterplots

Scatterplots are useful for associations between two variables in the same year.

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(assignment_sample == TRUE & year == 2023) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = gdp_per_capita_ppp, y = life_expectancy)) +
  geom_point(color = hks_blue, alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())) +
  labs(
    x = "GDP per capita, PPP",
    y = "Life expectancy at birth",
    title = "Income and Life Expectancy",
    subtitle = "Assignment-sample countries, 2023"
  )
```

This graph shows an association. It does not prove that GDP per capita causes
life expectancy.

## Color and facets

Color can show groups.

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(assignment_sample == TRUE & year == 2023) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = gdp_per_capita_ppp, y = life_expectancy, color = region)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())) +
  labs(
    x = "GDP per capita, PPP",
    y = "Life expectancy at birth",
    color = "Region",
    title = "Income and Life Expectancy by Region",
    subtitle = "Assignment-sample countries, 2023"
  )
```

Facets create small multiples.

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(assignment_sample == TRUE & year == 2023) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = gdp_per_capita_ppp, y = life_expectancy)) +
  geom_point(color = hks_blue, alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())) +
  facet_wrap(~region) +
  labs(
    x = "GDP per capita, PPP",
    y = "Life expectancy at birth",
    title = "Income and Life Expectancy by Region",
    subtitle = "Each panel uses the same 2023 country-year data"
  )
```

## Bar charts

Bar charts can compare values across countries in one year.

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(country %in% c("Ghana", "Kenya", "Rwanda", "Tanzania") & year == 2023) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(country, life_expectancy), y = life_expectancy)) +
  geom_col(fill = hks_blue) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Life expectancy at birth",
    title = "Life Expectancy Across Peer Countries",
    subtitle = "Four countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, 2023"
  )
```
